title: KMS/HSM key rotation canary + Vault<>SecretsManager sync terraform module
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Provide a reusable Terraform module that: (1) provisions cross-account AWS KMS keys and CloudHSM bindings suitable for Private/VPC deployments, (2) implements a safe, observable key rotation canary path, and (3) synchronizes critical secrets between HashiCorp Vault and AWS Secrets Manager for mixed-hosted/private customers. The module should be configurable for Secrets Manager-only, Vault-only, or hybrid sync modes; support automatic and manual rotation flows; emit healthcheck metrics; and include upgrade-compatible migration tooling so existing customers do not experience downtime during KMS upgrades.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terraform module API documented with inputs/outputs and examples for single-account, cross-account (operator-managed) and on-prem HSM binding.
- Rotation canary implementation: deploys a shadow key, re-encrypts a small sample of secrets, runs verification lambda (or integration test) and only promotes if checks pass. Failure paths roll back and alert.
- Vault sync: optional periodic reconciliation job that mirrors specific paths from Vault to Secrets Manager with metadata (version, last_sync). Supports soft-delete and TTL preservation where supported.
- Health checks: exported CloudWatch metrics and logs for rotation success/failure, sync lag, and last successful verification. Terraform exports alarms and dashboard pieces.
- Upgrade path: documented step-by-step and automated plan that can move customers from legacy KMS bindings to new module without needing app redeploys (using secondary encryption context and gradual rewrap strategy).
- Integration tests (terraform apply in a test account) and a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the canary flow against a sandbox before merge.

Non-goals: implementing Vault operator logic beyond reconciliation; building a proprietary HSM firmware integration.

Risks and trade-offs considered:
- AWS KMS multi-key approach vs single key policy: chose dual-key canary pattern to allow immediate rollback and to avoid broadly-scoped IAM policy churn.
- Secrets sync consistency: eventual consistency chosen (periodic reconciliation + version checks) to avoid tight coupling between Vault lifecycle and SecretsManager immediate behavior.
- HSM binding complexity: module will surface binding templates and rely on a small operator-run step for HSM cluster enrollment rather than automating cluster provisioning.

notes: Implementation details: module will expose an optional 'canary_scope' input that defines the secrets subset for test rewrap. It will optionally create a temporary Lambda (Go runtime) to run verification by decrypting and re-encrypting test payloads using both keys and asserting no data corruption.

Upgrade plan: 1) deploy canary keys via module, 2) schedule off-peak canary rewrap, 3) if successful, progressively increase canary_scope to full namespace, 4) promote new key by rotating alias and deprecate old key after N days. Backout: keep old key active until at least one successful promotion window or until rollback is triggered.
Operational alerts: on rotation failure raise PagerDuty SRE team; on sync_lag > 5m create a P0 incident if critical secrets are affected. Non-critical secrets (labels) only trigger warnings.

Follow-ups (ENG-15004): implement reconciliation retry/backoff and event-based trigger for Vault write-streams.
